**Statements:**

All bats are racquets.

questions.question: If 29 November 2009 is Sunday, then what will be the day of the week on 30 May 2010?
questions.solution:
There are 2 odd days in a month with 30 days and 3 odd days in a month with 31 days. Also, February with 28 days has 0 odd days and February with 29 days have 1 odd day.

Number of odd days between 29 November 2009 to 30 May 2010 = (1 + 3 + 3 + 0 + 3 + 2 + 30) = 42

42 when divided by 7, leaves 0 as remainder.

Sunday + 0 = Sunday

Hence, ‘**Sunday**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India still uses the ancient bamboo drip irrigation method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya** still uses the ancient **bamboo drip irrigation method**, which is a traditional method of irrigation that involves the use of **bamboo pipes** to supply water to crops. 
 
• Meghalaya's **unique topography**, with its hills and valleys, makes it well-suited for this method of irrigation as it allows for the** collection and distribution** of water to different levels of the terrain.
 
• This method is **eco-friendly, cost-effective,** and sustainable as it uses locally available resources and does not require electricity or fuel to operate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** primarily uses modern irrigation methods such as **sprinkler and drip irrigation. **
 
• **Maharashtra **also primarily uses **modern irrigation methods,** although some farmers may still use traditional methods on a small scale.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** primarily uses** canal irrigation** and **tube wells** for irrigation purposes.
 
• Bamboo drip irrigation is also known as the** "jingkieng ksiar"** method in Meghalaya and has been used for centuries by the** Khasi tribe.**
 
• The bamboo pipes used in this method are **perforated with small holes **to allow water to drip slowly onto the roots of the crops.
 
• Other traditional methods of irrigation used in India include the use of **bullock carts **to draw water from wells, the construction of **earthen embankments** to create ponds and the use of traditional water harvesting structures such as** stepwells and baolis.**

questions.question: Silicon doped with gallium forms ______.

__
 
• **Silicon **doped with** gallium** forms a** p-type semiconducto**r because gallium is a** trivalent impurity** and replaces some of the silicon atoms in the crystal lattice, creating a** hole** in the valence band.
 
• **P-type semiconductors** have a **majority of holes** as their charge carriers and a smaller number of **electrons,** which are the minority carriers.
 
• **N-type semiconductors,** on the other hand, are doped with a **pentavalent impurity** like phosphorus, which adds an extra electron to the conduction band and creates a **surplus of electrons** as the majority carriers.
 
• **Superconductors **are materials that exhibit **zero electrical resistance **below a certain** temperature, **and **silicon doped with gallium** is not known to exhibit superconductivity.
 
• **Insulators **are materials that do not conduct electricity at all and have a **very high resistance,** which is not the case with **p-type semiconductors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In a** p-type semiconductor**, the holes in the valence band can move from **one atom to another **and act as **positive charge carriers**, while the electrons in the conduction band are** immobile unless **excited by an external energy source. 
 
• The doping process is a way to intentionally introduce impurities into a **semiconductor crystal** to alter its electrical properties and enable the creation of **p-n junctions**, which are the basis of many **electronic devices.**
 
• Some common **p-type dopants** besides gallium are** boron and aluminum, **while common **n-type dopants** include **arsenic and antimony.**
 
• The properties of a semiconductor depend not only on its doping but also on its** temperature, light exposure**, and other environmental factors that can affect its **carrier concentration, mobility, and recombination.**
